18 An escalator in an underground station has 250 people standing on it and is moving with a
velocity of 4.3 m s–1. The average mass of a person is 78 kg and the angle of the escalator to the
horizontal is 40°.
What is the minimum power required to lift these people?
A
54 kW
B
64 kW
C
530 kW
D
630 kW

hints: Notice the escalator velocity of $4.3\text{ m s}^{-1}$ is along the $40^{\circ}$ slope, but lifting means gaining height, so you need the vertical part of that velocity.
Recall power against gravity can be written as weight times vertical speed: $P = mgv_{vertical}$, where $m$ is the total $250 \times 78\text{ kg}$ mass.
Calculate $v_{vertical} = 4.3\sin40^{\circ}\text{ m s}^{-1}$ and then multiply by total weight $mg$ with $g = 9.81\text{ m s}^{-2}$, then check the result in $\text{kW}$.
walkthrough: Find the total mass being lifted: $m = 250 \times 78 = 19500\text{ kg}$. The total weight is $W = mg$.

Only vertical motion increases gravitational potential energy, so resolve the slope velocity into a vertical component. The vertical side is opposite $40^{\circ}$, so $v_{vertical} = v\sin40^{\circ}$.
Use $P = \text{rate of work against weight} = Wv_{vertical} = mgv_{vertical}$ for minimum power at constant velocity.
Using $\cos40^{\circ}$ would give the horizontal speed and about $630\text{ kW}$, which does not lift the people. This is option C

A.explanation: About 10 times too small. It is close to the power for only about 25 people, suggesting a missing zero from $250 \times 78\text{ kg}$.

B.explanation: About 10 times too small and larger than A. It is close to using the horizontal component with too few people, not $v\sin40^{\circ}$ for all 250 people.

C.explanation: Equals the rate of gain of gravitational potential energy for total mass $19500\text{ kg}$ rising at $4.3\sin40^{\circ}\text{ m s}^{-1}$, about $5.3 \times 10^5\text{ W}$.

D.explanation: Uses $4.3\cos40^{\circ}$ instead of $4.3\sin40^{\circ}$. Cosine gives the horizontal velocity component, which does no work against weight.
